samples.question: This picture shows five coloured rings arranged in a closed chain; each ring overlaps its two neighbours, and every overlapping pair meets at exactly two crossings. At each crossing one of the two rings is drawn with a short break: the broken ring passes BEHIND, and the unbroken ring passes IN FRONT. Two rings are interlocked only when the order alternates between their two crossings, that is when each of them is in front at one crossing and behind at the other. If the same ring is in front at both of their crossings, that pair is not interlocked and the two rings could be pulled apart. Exactly one ring in the picture is not interlocked with either of its neighbours, so it could be lifted away from the chain. Which ring is that? Answer with its colour, one of: blue, brown, green, orange, purple, red.
